models.section: 4.2 Solution of the Wear Depth Distribution
models.family: bivariate-normal spatial surface with PSO fitting
models.purpose: Represent the image-derived stair-wear field and estimate its center, spread, and correlation parameters.
models.summary: A single-center bivariate normal density is used as a wear-depth surface, and five parameters are fitted by particle swarm optimization against the processed image field.

variables.unit: paper labels cm but image calibration is unspecified
cm in later cross-sections; pixels in processed image

variables.definition: Correlation parameter in the bivariate normal surface.

governing_equations.purpose: Define the single-center spatial wear surface.

equation_status.reason: Equation (1) was checked on the full-resolution PDF page 7 render.

objectives: Approximate the processed wear field with a compact spatial surface.
Provide a field consumed by the traffic and direction models.
constraints: Absolute value of rho_c must be below 1.
sigma_1 and sigma_2 must be positive.
The paper reduces the observed two-foot pattern to one wear center.

details: Static spatial fit has no time initial condition.
No stair-edge truncation or mass renormalization is stated.

parameter_estimation.method: Particle swarm optimization minimizes an unnormalized squared-error objective; the paper reports fitted rho_c, mu_1, mu_2, sigma_1, sigma_2 and error 35.562.

steps: Initialize particles in the five-parameter search space.
Evaluate squared error between model and observed field.
Update personal and global best positions.
Iterate to a stated maximum or error threshold.
algorithm.convergence_criteria: A maximum iteration count or error requirement is described generically, but numeric settings are omitted.

assumptions: One indentation adequately represents two nearly identical foot-placement indentations.
A single-person wear center represents the long-run surface.
The processed image values are comparable with physical depth.

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: No calibrated depth observations, residual map, alternative surface family, or repeated fit establishes that the five parameters are identifiable from the selected image.

models.computational_cost: Population size, iteration count, runtime, and seed policy are omitted.
strengths: Turns a spatial image into a compact field used consistently by later branches.
limitations: A normalized probability density is treated as wear depth without an amplitude parameter.
Metric scale and camera geometry are not calibrated.
One selected step and one local optimum are shown.

models.section: 5.1 Pedestrian Flow Calculation based on Archard's Law
models.purpose: Estimate average daily pedestrian traffic from accumulated wear.
models.summary: The paper states a power-law wear relation d=kN^b and integrates its inverse over the stair surface, divided by elapsed days, to obtain daily traffic.

variables.definition: Accumulated wear depth, spatially varying in Equation (3).
Empirical material and environment coefficient; prose later also calls 0.06 a friction coefficient.
Pedestrian count entering the wear law.
Elapsed time since completion, set to 238710 days.
Integration domain for a step surface; prose mentions the i-th step and total step count.

governing_equations.purpose: Relate cumulative pedestrian count to wear depth.
Invert the wear law over the stair surface to estimate mean daily traffic.

equation_status.reason: Equations (2)-(3) were checked on the full-resolution PDF page 10 render.

objectives: Estimate usage frequency in people per day.
Provide traffic inputs for the crowd and age models.
constraints: k and b are treated as constant over the whole surface and history.
T is fixed by a 1370 completion date.
The paper sets b=0.3, A=0.8 m^2, and k=0.06.

details: Integration is over A, but stair count and surface coordinate units are not implemented explicitly.

parameter_estimation.method: T and annual visitors are externally looked up; b is selected from a stated range; A is calculated geometrically; k=0.06 is assigned from a claimed marble friction coefficient.

steps: Evaluate fitted wear field over A.
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Numerical integration grid and tolerance are omitted.

assumptions: Wear is a stationary power law of count.
All pedestrians have equal load and sliding distance.
Material and environment do not vary over 654 years.
Repairs do not alter the accumulated field for this inversion.

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: One wear snapshot cannot separately identify age, count, load, material, environment, and repair effects; the chosen k also changes role between wear and friction coefficient.

models.computational_cost: Not reported; one surface integral is implied.
strengths: Makes the inverse calculation and parameter values visible.
Produces the requested daily usage quantity.
limitations: Equation (3) does not visibly sum over the stated n steps.
Coordinate, area, and depth units are not reconciled.
External visitor count has different scope from stair passages.

Wear depth at the edge reference location.

constraints: D>0 maps to more ascent, D<0 to more descent, and |D| approximately 0 to balance.
The original stair geometry is assumed symmetric enough for the contrast.

details: Reference points are selected from cross-sections rather than a PDE boundary.

parameter_estimation.method: No fitted parameter; two field values are read from the wear profile.

steps: Read d_edge and d_mid from a cross-section.
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Not applicable to a direct index.

models.section: 5.3 Walking Patterns Model based on Navier-Stokes Equations
models.family: source-augmented continuity PDE with finite differences
models.purpose: Estimate pedestrian density and classify single-file versus side-by-side travel.
models.summary: Pedestrians are treated as a continuous medium; a density continuity equation with source term is advanced using Forward Euler and central differences under a no-slip boundary.

variables.unit: paper states people/s; PDE requires density/time

governing_equations.source_expression: partial rho/partial t + div(rho v) = N(x,y,t)
governing_equations.purpose: Conserve pedestrian density with a source term.

governing_equations.source_expression: rho_i^(n+1)=rho_i^n-Delta_t[partial(rho v_x)/partial x + partial(rho v_y)/partial x]_i + Delta_t*N(x_i,y_j,t_n)
governing_equations.normalized_latex: \rho_i^{n+1}=\rho_i^n-\Delta t\left[\frac{\partial}{\partial x}(\rho v_x)+\frac{\partial}{\partial x}(\rho v_y)\right]_i+\Delta t\,N(x_i,y_j,t_n)
governing_equations.purpose: State the paper's Forward Euler update before spatial substitution.

governing_equations.source_expression: rho_(i,j)^(n+1)=rho_(i,j)^n-Delta_t[((rho v_x)_(i+1,j)^n-(rho v_x)_(i-1,j)^n)/(2 Delta_x)+((rho v_y)_(i,j+1)^n-(rho v_y)_(i,j-1)^n)/(2 Delta_y)] + Delta_t N_(i,j)^n
governing_equations.normalized_latex: \rho_{i,j}^{n+1}=\rho_{i,j}^{n}-\Delta t\left[\frac{(\rho v_x)_{i+1,j}^{n}-(\rho v_x)_{i-1,j}^{n}}{2\Delta x}+\frac{(\rho v_y)_{i,j+1}^{n}-(\rho v_y)_{i,j-1}^{n}}{2\Delta y}\right]+\Delta t\,N_{i,j}^{n}
governing_equations.purpose: Discretize flux divergence by central differences.
Impose the stated no-slip wall boundary.

equation_status.reason: Equations (5)-(8) were checked on full-resolution PDF pages 12-13.

objectives: Map density below 1.5 to single-file and 1.5-2.5 to two-person flow.
constraints: Crowd is continuous.
Velocity is zero at walls or obstacles.
The paper assigns N=1 for density below 1.5 and N=2 for density from 1.5 to 2.5.

details: No initial density field is stated.
No-slip v(x,y,t)=0 is printed, but the wall geometry is not specified.
No steady-state or stopping criterion is stated.

parameter_estimation.method: Velocity field, grid, time step, source field, and density-flow closure are not estimated from data.

steps: Approximate flux divergence by centered differences.
Read density and apply the class threshold.
algorithm.convergence_criteria: No CFL condition, grid convergence, end time, or stopping rule is reported.

assumptions: Pedestrians form a continuous medium.
Wall interaction is no-slip.
A source-flow rule is sufficient without a momentum or speed-density closure.
The density threshold identifies formation.

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: The paper provides neither trajectories nor density measurements; the reported rho=0.6535 conflicts with the Figure 11 color scale near 10^10.

models.computational_cost: Grid size, number of time steps, runtime, and solver settings are omitted.
strengths: Exposes state, flux, source, discretization, and boundary equations.
limitations: Equation (6) prints x derivatives for both flux components before Equation (7) uses y for the second.
Continuity alone is mislabeled as Navier-Stokes.
No stable numerical protocol or measured closure is provided.
